answer: Seats bind to a real phone line. Every 10 epochs the network calls each seat's number and reads a seed code the agent must post back within 5 minutes. A carrier line-type lookup rejects VoIP, so each extra identity needs its own SIM or copper landline at about $5 a month. A 200-key farm pays $1,000 monthly, and bulk SIMs bought in consecutive number ranges from one reseller act like a lantern: sequential blocks get merged into one seat. The voyage from one key to many stops being free.
